flags: W&T Offshore declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.01 per share of common stock for the fourth quarter of 2026, payable on November 19, 2026 to stockholders of record on November 12, 2026.

W&T Offshore reported third quarter 2026 operational and financial results, including a net loss of $13.6 million, or $(0.09) per diluted share, and Adjusted Net Income of $0.9 million, or $0.01 per diluted share.

W&T Offshore entered into the Second Amendment to its Credit Agreement, converting its $50.0 million revolving credit facility into a reserve-based revolving credit facility with an aggregate maximum credit amount of $100.0 million and eliminating the 75% excess cash flow sweep and $100.0 million minimum PDP PV-10 covenant.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 (P1) and Item 7 (P3).
business_model.claim: W&T Offshore, Inc. is an independent oil and natural gas producer operating offshore in the Gulf of America that derives revenue from selling oil, natural gas, and NGLs.
quotes: We are an independent oil and natural gas producer with substantially all our operations offshore in the Gulf of America.
Our revenues are derived from the sale of our oil and natural gas production, as well as the sale of NGLs.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations (F2).
business_model.claim: For the 9 Months Ended Sep. 30, 2026, total revenues were $ 479,718 (table in thousands), comprising $ 322,330 from oil, 123,184 from natural gas, 22,069 from NGLs, and $ 12,135 from other revenues.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Part I, Item 2 (P4).
business_model.claim: As of September 30, 2026, the company held working interests in 48 offshore fields covering approximately 588,500 gross acres (455,800 net acres) in federal and state waters, with a majority of daily production derived from wells it operates.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we hold working interests in 48 offshore fields in federal and state waters (which include 41 fields in federal waters and seven in state waters).

We currently have under lease approximately 588,500 gross acres (455,800 net acres) spanning across the outer continental shelf off the coasts of Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi and Alabama, with approximately 5,600 gross acres in Alabama state waters, 446,700 gross acres on the conventional shelf and approximately 136,200 gross acres in the deepwater.
A majority of our daily production is derived from wells we operate.

business_model.claim: The company sells its oil, NGLs, and natural gas to third-party customers under mostly short-term contracts at prices generally tied to monthly or daily indices quoted in industry publications.
quotes: We sell our oil, NGLs and natural gas to third-party customers.
The terms of sale under the majority of existing contracts are short-term, usually one year or less in duration.
The prices received for oil, NGL and natural gas sales are generally tied to monthly or daily indices as quoted in industry publications.

business_model.claim: In 2025, BP Products North America and Shell Trading (US) Company accounted for 33% and 17%, respectively, of oil, NGLs, and natural gas sales revenues, though management believes replacement customers could be obtained quickly due to the commoditized nature of the products.
quotes: In 2025, BP Products North America and Shell Trading (US) Company accounted for 33% and 17%, respectively, of our revenues from sales of oil, NGLs and natural gas.

Given the commoditized nature of the products we produce and market and the location of our production in the Gulf of America, we believe the loss of any of the customers above would not result in a material adverse effect on our ability to market future oil and natural gas production, as we believe that replacement customers could be obtained in a relatively short period of time on terms, conditions, and pricing substantially similar to those currently existing.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 (P1).
business_model.claim: The company operates in one reportable segment.
quotes: We operate in one reportable segment.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 (P3) and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 (P4).
business_model.claim: Revenues are primarily driven by oil, NGLs, and natural gas production volumes and realized sales prices, which differ from WTI oil and NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas benchmarks due to quality, location, transportation, and volume-weighting differentials.
quotes: Our financial condition, cash flow and results of operations are significantly affected by the volume of our oil, NGLs and natural gas production and the prices that we receive for such production.

Our average realized sales price for oil and natural gas differs from the WTI average price and the NYMEX Henry Hub average price, respectively, primarily due to premiums or discounts, quality adjustments, location adjustments and volume weighting (collectively referred to as differentials).

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 (P4).
business_model.claim: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, oil, NGL, and natural gas revenues increased by $36,567 (table in thousands) year over year—driven by $32,355 from price changes and $4,212 from volume changes—as production increased by 239 to 3,514 MBoe primarily due to a well recompletion at the Garden Banks 783 field.
quotes: Production volumes increased by 239 Mboe to 3,514 MBoe during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 primarily due to recompletion of a well at our Garden Banks 783 field.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 (P1), Item 1A (P2), and Item 7 (P3).
business_model.claim: Production and revenues are exposed to planned and unplanned downtime, Gulf of America storms, third-party infrastructure outages, and asset concentration—with Mobile Bay Properties accounting for approximately 36% of production and 20% of total revenue in 2025 while experiencing approximately 686 MBoe of deferred production from shut-ins out of approximately 2.5 MMBoe total deferred production in 2025.
quotes: For 2025, approximately 36% of our production and 20% of our total revenue was attributable to our interests in certain oil and natural gas leasehold interests and associated wells and units located off the coast of Alabama, in state coastal and federal Gulf of America waters approximately 70 miles south of Mobile, Alabama (the “Mobile Bay Properties”).
These shut-ins resulted in deferred production of approximately 686 MBoe based on production rates prior to the shut-ins.
For 2025, we estimate deferred production was approximately 2.5 MMBoe.
Tropical storms and hurricanes occur in the Gulf of America during the summer and fall, which can require us to evacuate personnel and shut in production until a storm subsides.

business_model.claim: Gulf of America proved reserves have relatively short reserve lives—with 34.0% of total proved reserves as of December 31, 2025 estimated to be depleted within three years—requiring ongoing capital investments or acquisitions to replace reserves and sustain revenue.
quotes: Our independent petroleum consultant estimates that 34.0% of our total proved reserves as of December 31, 2025 will be depleted within three years.

As a result, our need to replace proved reserves and production from new investments is relatively greater than that of producers who recover lower percentages of their proved reserves over a similar time period, such as those producers who have a larger portion of their proved reserves in areas other than the Gulf of America.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q financial statements (F2, F3) and MD&A (P4), and 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A (P2).
business_model.claim: The company uses commodity derivative positions to manage price volatility for a portion of future production, recording gains and losses outside revenues in Derivative loss (gain), net—resulting in a derivative loss of 42,230 and net derivative cash settlement outflows of (20,908) (tables in thousands) in the 9 Months Ended Sep. 30, 2026.
quotes: Our oil, NGL and natural gas revenues do not include the effects of derivatives, which are reported in Derivative loss (gain), net in our Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations.

While these commodity derivative positions are intended to reduce the effects of price volatility, they may also limit future income if prices were to rise substantially over the price established by such positions.

Impairments of our oil and gas properties are more likely to occur during prolonged periods of depressed oil, NGLs and natural gas pricing.

competitive_position.claim: W&T Offshore holds working interests in 48 offshore fields in federal and state waters across approximately 588,500 gross acres (455,800 net acres) in the Gulf of America and derives a majority of its daily production from wells it operates.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we hold working interests in 48 offshore fields in federal and state waters (which include 41 fields in federal waters and seven in state waters).

We currently have under lease approximately 588,500 gross acres (455,800 net acres) spanning across the outer continental shelf off the coasts of Louisiana, Texas, Mississippi and Alabama, with approximately 5,600 gross acres in Alabama state waters, 446,700 gross acres on the conventional shelf and approximately 136,200 gross acres in the deepwater.
A majority of our daily production is derived from wells we operate.

competitive_position.claim: W&T Offshore owns an existing portfolio of 200 structures, of which it operates 142, and operates 86.7% of its wells, which reduces capital expenditures and maximizes returns on capital expenditures when developing prospects.
quotes: Our existing portfolio of 200 structures (142 of which we operate) provides a key advantage when evaluating and developing prospect opportunities and serves to reduce capital expenditures and maximize our returns on capital expenditures.
As of December 31, 2025, we operate 86.7% of our wells.

competitive_position.claim: The company's Gulf of America offshore reservoirs feature high porosity and permeability with higher initial production rates than other domestic reservoirs, natural drive mechanisms requiring fewer conventional wells, and some of the lowest greenhouse gas emissions intensity due to subsea wells and established pipelines.
quotes: The reservoirs in our offshore fields are generally characterized as having high porosity and permeability, with higher initial production rates relative to other domestic reservoirs.
Fewer conventional wells are required to develop these fields.

Production from the Gulf of America continues to provide some of the lowest greenhouse gas (“GHG”) emissions intensity due to the nature of subsea wells and established offshore pipelines, and we continue to strive to lower our GHG emissions.

competitive_position.claim: As a smaller oil and natural gas company, W&T Offshore asserts greater decision-making flexibility, faster adaptation to market changes, potential for higher profit margins on smaller projects, and alignment through significant insider ownership.
quotes: As a smaller oil and natural gas company, however, we have greater flexibility in decision making, can adapt quicker to market changes, have the potential for higher profit margins on smaller projects and have the opportunity to develop innovative strategies without the constraints of large-scale operations.

Our significant inside ownership ensures that executive management’s interests are highly aligned with those of our shareholders, thus incentivizing executive management to maximize value and mitigate risk in executing our business strategy, generating shareholder value.

competitive_position.claim: BP Products North America and Shell Trading (US) Company accounted for 33% and 17% of oil, NGL, and natural gas sales revenues, though the company states it could replace them quickly on substantially similar terms.
quotes: In 2025, BP Products North America and Shell Trading (US) Company accounted for 33% and 17%, respectively, of our revenues from sales of oil, NGLs and natural gas.

Given the commoditized nature of the products we produce and market and the location of our production in the Gulf of America, we believe the loss of any of the customers above would not result in a material adverse effect on our ability to market future oil and natural gas production, as we believe that replacement customers could be obtained in a relatively short period of time on terms, conditions, and pricing substantially similar to those currently existing.

competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter production rose to 38.2 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (up 10% sequentially and 7% year-over-year), while nine-month Adjusted EBITDA reached $163.9 million (up 50% year-over-year) and nine-month Free Cash Flow reached $89.3 million.
quotes: Produced 38.2 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day (“MBoe/d”) (50% liquids), which was approximately 9% above midpoint and 4% above the high end of the Company’s guidance and up 10% from the second quarter of 2026;

Generated Adjusted EBITDA of $51.1 million, an increase of 30% over the third quarter of 2025 and $163.9 million of Adjusted EBITDA generated in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 50% compared to the first nine months of 2025;
Generated Free Cash Flow of $33.2 million for the third quarter of 2026 and $89.3 million for the first nine months of 2026;

competitive_position.claim: Available liquidity reached $234.7 million with Net Debt down to $160.7 million (0.9 times trailing twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA), and W&T converted its revolving credit facility into a reserve-based lending structure with an aggregate maximum credit amount of $100.0 million and initial elected commitments of $50.0 million.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, W&T had available liquidity of $234.7 million comprised of $191.3 million in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents and $43.4 million of borrowing availability under W&T’s revolving credit facility, based on a borrowing base of $50.0 million and $6.6 million of letters of credit outstanding.
As of September 30, 2026, the Company had total debt of $352.0 million, Net Debt of $160.7 million and Net Debt to trailing twelve month Adjusted EBITDA was 0.9 times.

On October 1, 2026, we entered into the Amended Credit Agreement, pursuant to which our revolving credit facility was converted into a reserve-based revolving credit facility, with an aggregate maximum credit amount of $100.0 million and an aggregate elected commitment amount initially set at $50.0 million.

competitive_position.claim: W&T faces intense competition from larger domestic, foreign, and independent oil companies that have substantially greater financial, technical, and personnel resources to bid for BOEM leases, acquire properties, absorb regulatory assurance burdens, and withstand commodity downturns.
quotes: Many of these competitors are large, well-established companies that have financial and other resources substantially greater than ours.
For example, new leases acquired from the BOEM are acquired through a “sealed bid” process and are generally awarded to the highest bidder.
Finally, companies with larger financial resources may have a significant advantage in terms of meeting any potential new bonding or financial assurance requirements.

competitive_position.claim: Because Gulf of America proved reserves have shorter reserve lives, an independent petroleum consultant estimated that 34.0% of W&T's total proved reserves will be depleted within three years, creating greater capital-intensive reserve replacement needs.
quotes: Our independent petroleum consultant estimates that 34.0% of our total proved reserves as of December 31, 2025 will be depleted within three years.

As a result, our need to replace proved reserves and production from new investments is relatively greater than that of producers who recover lower percentages of their proved reserves over a similar time period, such as those producers who have a larger portion of their proved reserves in areas other than the Gulf of America.

competitive_position.claim: Consolidation and decommissioning of midstream gathering, pipeline, and processing assets in the Gulf of America threaten W&T's ability to market production, with fields holding approximately 1.0 MMBoe (or 0.8%) of proved reserves tied back to third-party platforms.
quotes: In recent years, we have seen a consolidation of gathering systems, pipelines and processing facilities in the Gulf of America, which has led to fewer midstream counterparties to contract with for transportation and processing.
A reduction in the number of potential midstream counterparties and available midstream infrastructure could negatively impact our ability to market production.
As of December 31, 2025, two fields, accounting for approximately 1.0 MMBoe (or 0.8%) of our total proved reserves, are tied back to separate, third-party owned platforms.

competitive_position.claim: All current production is concentrated in the Gulf of America—exposed to hurricanes and shared regional disruptions—with approximately 36% of production and 20% of total revenue concentrated in Mobile Bay Properties, where shut-ins deferred approximately 686 MBoe of production.
quotes: All of our current production is from the Gulf of America.

For 2025, approximately 36% of our production and 20% of our total revenue was attributable to our interests in certain oil and natural gas leasehold interests and associated wells and units located off the coast of Alabama, in state coastal and federal Gulf of America waters approximately 70 miles south of Mobile, Alabama (the “Mobile Bay Properties”).
These shut-ins resulted in deferred production of approximately 686 MBoe based on production rates prior to the shut-ins.

competitive_position.claim: Regulatory financial assurance requirements from BOEM and ongoing surety litigation over collateral demands—where mediation reached an impasse with non-settling sureties despite approximately $94 million in withdrawn demands from USSIC and PIIC and a $105 million preliminary injunction denial recommendation—could materially constrain liquidity and capital spending.
quotes: The future cost of compliance with respect to supplemental financial assurances, including the obligations imposed on us, whether as current or predecessor lessee or grant holder in respect of BOEM’s final rule or any new, more stringent, rules related to supplemental financial assurances could materially and adversely affect our financial condition, cash flows, liquidity and results of operations.
The entry into the Settlement Agreements resulted in the withdrawal of approximately $94 million in collateral demands.
The preliminary injunction would have required us to immediately post $105 million of collateral.
Mediation is no longer active as the mediator has declared an impasse with respect to the surety providers that did not enter into the Settlement Agreements.

competitive_position.claim: Sustained declines in oil, NGL, and natural gas prices threaten W&T's cash flows, capital expenditure funding, borrowing capacity, proved reserve volumes, and full-cost ceiling-test carrying values.
quotes: Extended periods of lower prices for oil, NGLs and natural gas can have a material adverse impact on our results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.

While we have not recorded an impairment of our oil and gas properties during 2025, any further decreases in commodity pricing could cause an impairment, which would result in a non-cash charge to earnings.

competitive_position.claim: Deep shelf and deepwater drilling carry higher costs and mechanical failure risks, while W&T lacks business interruption insurance and could fall behind better-funded competitors if it cannot adopt new exploration and seismic technologies at acceptable cost.
quotes: We do not carry business interruption insurance.
There are additional risks associated with deep shelf and deepwater drilling that could result in substantial cost overruns and/or result in uneconomic projects or wells.

In addition, competitors may have greater financial, technical and personnel resources that allow them to enjoy technological advantages, and that may in the future, allow them to implement new technologies before we can.
